pending_commit.commit_message: FROMLIST: mmc: sdhci: Add support for O2 eMMC HS200 mode When use eMMC as boot device, the eMMC signaling voltage is tied to 1.8v fixed output voltage, bios can set o2 sd host controller PCI configuration register 0x308 bit4 to 1 to let driver skip 3.3v signaling voltage and direct use 1.8v singling voltage in eMMC initialize process. Changes: Check PCIe register 0x308 bit 4 and skip eMMC 3.3v initialization process if it is set to 1. Conflicts: drivers/mmc/host/sdhci-pci-o2micro.c drivers/mmc/host/sdhci-pci-o2micro.h [craigb] defines moved to header file. BUG=b:71875355 TEST=Booted on grunt proto device with BAY_HUB_EN rework. Change-Id: I4091f300d7505fb2628bbc9dcc075e54eee14075 Signed-off-by: ernest.zhang <ernest.zhang@bayhubtech.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/959582 Commit-Ready: Craig Bergstrom <craigb@chromium.org> Tested-by: Craig Bergstrom <craigb@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: mmc: sdhci: Add support for O2 hardware tuning Add hardware tuning function instead of software tuning because O2/Bayhub SD host controller support hardware tuning. Changes: Add many functions to execute hardware tuning for eMMC 1.8V HS200 mode, the hardware tuning command and procedure is based on O2/Bayhub hardware tuning spec. Conflicts: drivers/mmc/host/sdhci-pci-o2micro.c drivers/mmc/host/sdhci.c [craigb] Did not apply cleanly, applied by hand. BUG=b:71875355 TEST=Booted on grunt proto device with BAY_HUB_EN rework. image_test: Remove check that kernel is not ELF. The associated change, CL:657262, removes the vmlinuz kernel from the base image to save space. In making this change, it was noiticed that the image_test runs lddtree.ParseELF() on the vmlinuz file. This raises an ELFError (as expected). Since it's unclear why this is being done, and it doesn't really make sense, this change removes this check. BUG=chromium:461595 TEST=Passed a trybot. CQ-DEPEND=CL:657262 Change-Id: I6b5695ee5477b44ddf0056bbdcfb3fc4ec8e05d8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/669605 Commit-Ready: Craig Bergstrom <craigb@chromium.org> Tested-by: Craig Bergstrom <craigb@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Craig Bergstrom <craigb@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Remove bulky vmlinu[zx] from rootfs. vmlinuz is several megabytes and does not need to live in chromeos's base partition because it's actually booted off of a kernel partition. This change removes the kernel from the base image to save space. BUG=chromium:461595 TEST=Built and installed on single chromebook. common-mk: Don't include sources in inputs for generating dbus bindings. Tip-of-tree GYP doesn't allow ${source} to end up in the inputs list. generate-dbus-adaptors.gypi and generate-dbus-proxies.gypi supply the sources as inputs, which are translated into ${source} at ninja generation time, causing assert failures with ToT GYP. Providing these as inputs does not appear to be necessary, and other generator .gypi files do not, so remove them to allow ToT GYP to be used. BUG=chromium:821283 TEST=Built cros-disks, cryptohome and permission_broker TEST=Check incremental rebuild triggers when modifying dbus sources: Build cryptohome with ninja touch cryptohome/dbus_adaptors/org.chromium.BootLockboxInterface.xml rerun ninja and the dbus bindings are regenerated Change-Id: Ibac6debe8d281fe93837e4339411c5ff0169d348 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/959844 Commit-Ready: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

chromeos-cr50-scripts: Factory shim need to handle noop return code and update URL of server The cr50-reset script interprets a NOOP returned from gsctool as an error, resulting in the gsctool printing a success message and the script printing a fail message. The URL to the Authorization server was incorrect. BRANCH=none BUG=b:74411523 TEST=Manually tested on an EVE device. The QRcode had the correct URL and the CR50 was reset after entering a proper challenge. After entering an incorrect challenge, the system displayed an error message. A new QRcode was generated after three incorrectly entered challenges.
